checks.assessment: 1911/4.1 K mercury observation is correctly historical and source-attributed. The resistance, current, kelvin and alloy explanations provide local entry points without changing the observation.

The Meissner effect is distinguished from merely having zero electrical resistance. Field exclusion is expressly limited to suitable weak-field conditions; an ideal perfect conductor is not automatically a superconductor.

The source's below-20-K range is not asserted to cover every material. Different transition conditions and the warning that cold alone is insufficient preserve the intended limitation. The general higher-temperature statement is not a claim about a fresh discovery.

Persistent current is conditional on an unbroken ring, maintained superconducting state, no disturbance/dissipation, and appropriate temperature, field and current limits. Ordinary resistive decay is retained; no unconditional perpetual-current claim remains.

No resistance heating is confined to steady current in a closed superconducting coil. The text separately acknowledges energy for establishing current/field and for cooling; it does not claim a whole electromagnet consumes no energy.

Strong-field destruction is tied to material-dependent critical conditions, not an inability of all superconducting magnets to make strong fields. Induced current is tied to a changing field, not field strength alone. Self-field, critical current and operating-condition dependence are retained.
Computer memory is explicitly a use reported for computers of the source's time. It is not presented as the usual memory technology of current computers.

Near-room-temperature transmission remains the book's hypothetical. Avoided losses are specifically ideal steady-DC wire resistance losses under maintained superconductivity and critical limits. AC/changing-field losses in the wire and other whole-system losses remain explicit.
1957 is limited to a microscopic explanation of conventional superconductivity, not completion of every material's explanation. No unrequested microscopic derivation or all-material theory is added.

scienceAssessment.limitations: This is the lesson's intentionally limited model, not exhaustive treatment of field penetration, mixed states, flux motion, material-specific phase diagrams or modern superconductivity research. No current discovery, room-temperature achievement or experimentally universal historical transition number was newly verified.
